alt="Archiving a session from the session dropdown context menu" style="max-width:100%;"> Keep your active session list clean by archiving old conversations instead of deleting them. You can archive a session by right-clicking on the session dropdown (not expanding it) and then selecting Archive. This hides it from the session dropdown but keeps it saved on the server. You can toggle the visibility of archived sessions by clicking the eye icon on the toolbar to the left of the dropdown. There is also a toolbar button to archive the session, you can use either option. > [[Session Dropdown Menu]] > [[Message History]] > [[Renaming the session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Options Panel Reference</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Customise the plugin behavior by navigating to `Tools > Options > Assistant`. Here, you can configure the path to the OpenCode binary, add process arguments, set a global system Preamble for all sessions, and toggle **Local Echo** for instant message rendering. You can also adjust UI preferences like toolbar icon size, chat font size, enable or disable specific features (like Stash Diff or Jump to file), and set a custom user avatar. Additionally, the plugin includes a background **Update Checker Service** that automatically queries for new releases (with randomised intervals between 16 and 24 hours). You can toggle the update checks under `Tools > Options > Assistant > Check for updates`. When an update is found, you will be prompted with a dialog to download the update immediately, get reminded later, or skip the version entirely. This page describes every preference in the panel, organised into six sections. All changes take effect when you click **Apply** or **OK**. ##### 1. Assistant Service <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Path to Opencode Binary</strong></td><td>Auto-detected</td><td>The full path to the OpenCode executable. If left blank, the plugin searches your <code>PATH</code>. If OpenCode is not found, a muted hint shows <em>"opencode not found on PATH"</em>. Use <strong>Browse...</strong> to pick a binary. Invalid paths show a validation error (e.g. <em>File not found</em>, <em>File is not executable</em>).</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Process Arguments</strong></td><td><code>acp</code></td><td>Extra command-line arguments passed when launching the OpenCode server process.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Launch through WSL (Windows only)</strong></td><td>Off</td><td>When enabled, all OpenCode invocations (the ACP server and token-usage stats) are wrapped through <strong>WSL</strong> using <code>wsl.exe</code>. The resolved Windows executable is automatically translated to its WSL mount path, so custom/WinGet/Choco-shim install locations resolve correctly. If OpenCode is installed as a native Linux binary inside WSL (no Windows executable found), it is invoked directly on the WSL PATH. Recommended when running OpenCode on Windows for best performance and bash compatibility.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Browse...</strong></td><td>—</td><td>Opens a file chooser to select the OpenCode executable.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 2. Updates <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Check for Updates</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Enables the background <strong>Update Checker Service</strong>, which queries for new releases at randomised intervals between 16 and 24 hours. When an update is found you can download it immediately, get reminded later, or skip that version.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 3. Chat Behavior <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Echo user input immediately (Local Echo)</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Renders your message instantly in the chat while the server is processing, instead of waiting for the first response.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Session Idle Timeout (seconds)</strong></td><td>600</td><td>How long (0–3600, step 5) a request may sit idle — with no data arriving from the server — before it is failed. This is an <em>idle</em> timeout, not an absolute deadline, so long-running responses that keep streaming are never cut off.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Combine tool and thought bubbles into a single accordion</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Groups tool outputs and reasoning into one expandable header instead of separate bubbles. Changing this reloads the current session.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Auto-backup uncommitted changes on turn start (git/hg) (Experimental)</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Stashes uncommitted changes in git/hg repositories before each turn, so the AI can be rolled back safely.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Max Messages</strong></td><td>100</td><td>The maximum number of visible bubbles (10–200, step 5) kept in the chat panel before older ones are trimmed from the view to conserve memory. The full history remains on the server and can be reloaded.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 4. Actions <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Enable Sort Lines editor context menu actions</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>Sort Lines Ascending</strong> and <strong>Sort Lines Descending</strong> items to the editor's right-click context menu.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Minify JSON editor context menu action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>Minify JSON</strong> item to the editor's right-click context menu for stripping formatting whitespace from JSON.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Search Web editor context menu action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>Search Web</strong> item to the editor's right-click context menu for searching the selected text (or the word under the cursor) on Google.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Toggle Annotations editor context menu action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>Toggle Annotations</strong> item to the editor's right-click context menu for toggling the versioning system's blame annotations.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable View File History editor context menu action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Adds the <strong>View File History</strong> item to the editor's right-click context menu for opening the versioning system's history view.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Stash Diff toolbar button and action</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Enables the <strong>Stash Diff</strong> toolbar button and the <code>Ctrl + Shift + L</code> action for viewing git stash diffs.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Jump to file dialog</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Enables the <strong>Jump to File</strong> dialog (a shortcut, e.g. <code>Ctrl + Alt + J</code>, is shown next to the label when one is available).</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Enable Mini Assistant</strong></td><td>On</td><td>Decides where <strong>Send to Assistant</strong> / <strong>Ask Assistant</strong> actions open: the floating mini dialog (enabled) or the main sidebar (disabled).</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 5. Appearance <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Custom User Icon (PNG)</strong></td><td>(empty)</td><td>Path to a PNG used as your avatar in chat. Click <strong>Browse...</strong> to pick one, or right-click the preview to clear it. Changing it reloads the session.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Toolbar Icon Size (requires restart)</strong></td><td>24</td><td>Icon size for the assistant toolbar: 16, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, or 48. Requires an IDE restart to apply.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Chat Font Size</strong></td><td>Inherited</td><td>Font size for chat text: Inherited (uses the theme), or 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> ##### 6. Session Preamble <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Preference</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Session preamble</strong></td><td>Bundled default</td><td>Sent as the first user message for new chats. Use <code>---</code> on its own line as a message separator. Right-click the text area to <strong>Clear</strong> it or <strong>Reset to default</strong>.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> > [[Post Install]] > [[OpenCode Not Installed]] > [[Update Notifications]] > [[Auto-Backup on Turn Start]] > [[Message History]] / [[Pinned Messages]] > [[Jump to File]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Mini Assistant]] / [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Customising the Toolbar]] > [[Starting a Session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Attachments</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> You can attach files and images to provide more context to the AI. Click the **Paperclip icon** in the input area to open the attachment menu. The paperclip icon displays a numeric badge showing how many files are currently attached, so attachments are visible at a glance. The plugin also supports dragging and dropping files directly into the chat, as well as pasting screenshots straight from your clipboard (provided you are using a vision-capable model). > [[Swing Mockups via Matisse]] > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]] > [[Chat Features]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Configuration Template</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> ##### opencode.json This is the starter configuration the plugin writes when you accept the global-config setup prompt. It lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (or `opencode.jsonc` on the JSONC variant): <pre><code> ` { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "autoupdate": false, "permission": { "read": { "~/.ssh/**": "deny", "~/.gnupg/**": "deny", "~/.aws/**": "deny", "~/.azure/**": "deny", "~/.kube/**": "deny", "~/.docker/**": "deny", "~/.config/gcloud/**": "deny", ".env*": "deny", "*.pem": "deny", "*.key": "deny", "*.p12": "deny", "*.jks": "deny", "*.jceks": "deny", "*.keystore": "deny", "*.kdbx": "deny", "*.pfx": "deny", "*.p8": "deny", "*credentials*": "deny", "*": "allow" }, "edit": { "~/.aws/**": "deny", "~/.azure/**": "deny", "~/.ssh/**": "deny", "~/.gnupg/**": "deny", "~/.kube/**": "deny", "~/.docker/**": "deny", "~/.config/gcloud/**": "deny", "*credentials*": "deny", "*.env*": "deny", "*": "ask" }, "bash": { "git add": "ask", "git rm": "ask", "git reset": "ask", "git commit": "ask", "git push": "ask", "rm": "ask" }, "webfetch": "allow", "websearch": "allow", "doom_loop": "ask" } } ` </code></pre> > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Unix Config]] / [[Windows Config]] > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]] > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]] > [[Global Configuration Setup]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Chat Features</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The chat panel is packed with features to help you get the most out of the assistant. alt="Mini Assistant" style="max-width:100%;"> The **Mini Assistant** is a compact, floating chat dialog that gives you quick access to the AI without needing the full sidebar panel. It shares the same session as the main assistant, so conversations stay in sync. You can disable it entirely under `Options > Assistant > Actions > Enable Mini Assistant` — when disabled, "Send to Assistant" / "Ask Assistant" actions open the main sidebar instead. > [[Opening the Ai6EWETdCPCJuhGhE3QjQiboJv/Ado4SIzPSTzGAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC" alt="Check token usage" style="max-width:100%;"> Click the **Currency/Token Stats** icon on the toolbar to see how many tokens your current session has used. Hover over the status label (which normally says "Ready") to view the context window fill level. This helps you decide when to run `/compact` to summarise the conversation and free up context. > [[Resetting context limits (/compact)]] > [[Time to first token]] > [[Customising the Toolbar]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Commands</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Slash commands let you perform quick actions directly from the chat input. Type `/` in the input area to trigger the autocomplete popup. Local commands handled entirely by the plugin (never sent to the server): * `/new` — start a new session (shows a project picker when multiple projects are open) * `/title My Title` — rename the current session directly; `/title` without arguments asks the AI to suggest and apply a title * `/archive` — toggle archiving (hiding) the current session * `/model` / `/models` — open the model selector * `/agents` — open the agent selector * `/level` — open the thinking-level selector * `/sessions` — open the session dropdown Server commands (e.g. `/compact`, `/dcp`) are forwarded to the OpenCode agent and appear in the same popup — `/compact` is listed there since v1.12.10. Note: the Mini Assistant hides the selectors (`/model`, `/models`, `/agents`, `/level`, `/sessions`); use the main panel or keyboard shortcuts for those. Each command links to a fuller explanation: > `/new` — [[Starting a Session]] > `/models`, `/agents`, `/level` — [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] > `/sessions` — [[Session Dropdown Menu]] > `/archive` — [[Archiving Sessions]] > `/title` — [[Renaming the session]] > `/compact` — [[Resetting context limits (/compact)]] > Typing `/` — [[Slash Command Autocomplete]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Slash Command Autocomplete</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Typing `/` in the input area opens an autocomplete popup listing all available commands — the plugin's local commands plus the server commands advertised by the OpenCode agent. Keep typing to narrow the list. Use Up/Down to highlight an entry, then press `Enter` or `Tab` to insert the highlighted command into the input. If the typed text exactly matches a command name, pressing `Enter` sends it immediately. The popup disappears when you press `Escape`, type a space, or click away. See [[Commands]] for the full list of available commands and what each one does.<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Input Area Keys</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The chat input area supports these keyboard shortcuts: <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Shortcut</th><th>Action</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><code>Enter</code></td><td>Send the message</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Shift + Enter</code></td><td>Insert a newline</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Tab</code></td><td>Switch agent / open the options panel</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Alt + Up</code> / <code>Alt + Down</code></td><td>Recall previous / next message from history</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + R</code></td><td>Open the History Search dialog (type to filter, Up/Down to navigate)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + Z</code> / <code>Ctrl + Y</code></td><td>Undo / redo</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Escape</code></td><td>Close popups and refocus the input</td></tr> </tbody> </table> > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] > [[Message History]] > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Slash Command Autocomplete]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Ask Assistant Menu</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Two editor menu entries launch the Mini Assistant for refactoring help: * Right-click in the editor and choose **Refactoring > Ask Assistant...** to send the current selection to the assistant for refactoring. * Use the code generator — press `Alt + Insert` (or open the Insert Code menu) and pick **Ask Assistant** to generate code from a prompt. Both open (or focus) the Mini Assistant with your selected code attached as context. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Attachments]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Inspector Context Menu</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> After running inspections (e.g. via `Analyze > Inspect & Transform`), right-click any item in the **Inspector** window to see two actions: * **Copy** — copies the selected subtree (filename, line number and description of each problem) to the clipboard as text. * **💬 Send to Assistant** — pre-fills the Mini Assistant input with the same text, so you can edit it before sending. The same **Copy** / **💬 Send to Assistant** actions are also available in the **Test Results** window on failed tests. > [[Test Results Context Menu]] > [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Send to Assistant</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The **💬 Send to Assistant** context action sends code or file context straight into the assistant for you to refine before sending: * **Editor:** Right-click selected code in the editor and choose **Send to Assistant** to open the assistant with the selection pre-filled. * **Projects / Explorer:** Right-click a file node and choose **Send to Assistant** to send that file's path as context. * **Inspector / Test Results:** Right-click an inspection problem or a failed test to send its details for diagnosis. Repeated sends **append** to the input instead of replacing it, so you can gather several snippets before sending. Which assistant opens (the floating Mini Assistant or the main sidebar) is controlled by the **Enable Mini Assistant** checkbox under `Options > Assistant > Actions`. When context-menu additions are disabled there, these actions hide from the menus. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Ask Assistant Menu]] > [[Inspector Context Menu]] / [[Test Results Context Menu]] > [[Options Panel Reference]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Test Results Context Menu</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> After running a test suite, right-click any failed test (or failure tree) in the **Test Results** window to access two actions: * **Copy** — copies the selected failure subtree (test name, file, line and failure message) to the clipboard as text. * **💬 Send to Assistant** — pre-fills the Mini Assistant input with the same text so you can ask for a diagnosis or fix. These actions share the same popup helper (`TreePopupSupport`) as the Inspector window. > [[Inspector Context Menu]] > [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Jump to File</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> alt="Jump to File dialog for searching files across open projects" style="max-width:100%;"> The **Jump to File** dialog (`Ctrl + Alt + J`, or `Cmd + Option + J` on Mac) lets you open any file across all open projects by typing part of its name. It matches case-insensitively by filename prefix, path substring, or glob patterns. Navigate with the arrow keys and press `Enter` to open. The dialog is backed by an in-memory index that rebuilds in the background and updates live as files change; it respects `.gitignore` and skips common directories like `node_modules/`, `target/`, and `build/`. Enable or disable it under `Options > Assistant`. > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[IDE Enhancements]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: alt="Message pinning" style="max-width:100%;"> Assistant messages can be pinned so they stay visible even as older messages are trimmed from the chat. Hover over an assistant bubble and click the pin icon to pin (or unpin) it. Pins are stored per session and persist across restarts, making it easy to keep a plan or to-do list on screen while the rest of the conversation scrolls away. > [[Message History]] > [[Filtering Chat 1;">Session Dropdown Menu</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Right-click a session in the session dropdown to get a quick action menu: * **Rename** — give the session a custom name * alt="New Session Confirm Bar" style="max-width:100%;"> When you start a new session, a slide-in confirmation bar appears above the input area: *"Select the agent, model and level below, then click Continue."* The agent, model, and thinking-level dropdowns stay locked until you confirm your selection, so the session starts with the configuration you intend. Clicking **Continue** unlocks the dropdowns and starts the session. > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Auto-Backup on Turn Start</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Before each turn, the plugin can back up your uncommitted changes by stashing them (git stash, or hg shelve for Mercurial) so work can be rolled back safely if the AI makes unwanted modifications. The backup appears as an **Auto-Backup** tool bubble in the chat. This is enabled by default under `Options > Assistant > Chat Behavior > Auto-backup uncommitted changes on turn start (git/hg) (Experimental)` and can be disabled there. > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Thinking and Tool Responses]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">OpenCode Not Installed</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If the plugin can't find the `opencode` binary, the chat panel shows an install-help bubble instead of the normal input: * A copyable, OS-specific install command (e.g. `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install.sh | sh` on Linux, `brew install opencode` on macOS, `winget install SST.opencode` on Windows) * A **View OpenCode Setup Guide** button * A **Restart Server** button * A note to open the Assistant settings via the gear icon above the message if OpenCode is already installed Clicking **Restart Server** re-checks for the binary. If it still isn't found, the bubble stays in place so you can try again; if it is found, the server starts and the bubble is replaced by the normal chat input. After installing OpenCode — and optionally setting the binary path under `Options > Assistant` — click **Restart Server** to connect. > [[macOS/Linux]] / [[Windows]] > [[Post Install]] > [[Restarting the server]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Troubleshooting]] > [[Global Configuration Setup]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Update Notifications</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The plugin checks for new releases in the background at randomised 16–24 hour intervals. When an update is available, a dialog offers three choices: * **Download Now** — open the release to download and install * **Remind me Later** * **Skip this Version** Disable the check under `Options > Assistant > Updates > Check for Updates`. > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Post Install]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Customising the Toolbar</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Right-click anywhere on the assistant toolbar to open the **Edit ToolBar** popup, which lists every toolbar button with a checkbox. Uncheck buttons you don't use (e.g. export, restart, mini assistant) and they disappear; check them again to restore. Your choices are saved and persist across IDE restarts. The toolbar provides quick access to actions like starting a session, viewing this guide, opening keyboard shortcuts, checking token usage, restarting the server, and exporting conversations. The icon size is set separately under `Options > Assistant > Appearance > Toolbar Icon Size`. > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Mini Assistant]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Markdown Project Type</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> **Markdown Project** is a minimal project type for folders of plain text, notes, or documentation — no compiler or build system needed. To create one, choose `Tools > New Project > Other > Markdown Project`, or just run `touch .mdproject` inside any folder to make it loadable as a project. It renders a clean directory tree in the Projects tab, filters OS junk and editor swap files, and can be closed or deleted from the project node's right-click menu. It's a handy workspace for chatting about a folder of text files — and for managing your OpenCode configuration. > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]] > [[IDE Enhancements]] > [[Experiments]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If you have strict privacy requirements or want to avoid API costs, you can run the plugin entirely offline using local LLMs: 1. Install a local runner like [Ollama](https://ollama.com) and download a coding model (e.g., `ollama run deepseek-coder` or `ollama run qwen2.5-coder`). 2. Add a configuration block for the local model in your `opencode.json` configuration file. Note that Qwen models might require `--think=false` if configured via Ollama, and a `"reasoningEffort": "none"` entry. 3. Open the chat options panel (click the gear icon or press `Tab` in the input area) and choose your local model from the dropdown list. All code queries and indexing tasks will now execute locally on your machine. > [[Configuration Template]] > [[Install Ollama]] > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Copying a message</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> You can copy individual user messages back into the input text-area. Hover over the user icon, it'll change into a copy button — clicking it copies the message to the clipboard and adds it to the input text-area so you can resend or edit it. Assistant responses can be copied by hovering over the bubble, you'll see a copy and a pin button, copy will copy to the clipboard. > [[Pinned Messages]] > [[Message History]] > [[Starting a Session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Experiments</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Here are some interesting things you can try with the plugin: > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]] > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Local Data Analysis in Java]] > [[Swing Mockups via Matisse]] > [[Markdown Project Type]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Exporting a conversation</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The share button on the toolbar exports the session to a file. Clicking it opens a small menu where you can choose between **Markdown** and **HTML** — HTML output mimics the sidebar chat view, including the expandable activity panels and chat styling. > [[Customising the Toolbar]] > [[Message History]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Filtering Chat Messages</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> To reduce clutter in your chat history, you can selectively show or hide different message types using the **Filter** button on the toolbar. Clicking this button opens a dropdown menu allowing you to toggle the visibility of: * **Activity**: Hides or shows tool outputs and internal model reasoning chains together. * **Assistant**: Hides or shows the assistant's responses. * **User**: Hides or shows your own messages. If the option to combine tools and thoughts is disabled in your settings, the menu will dynamically update to show individual checkboxes for **Tool** outputs and **Thought** reasoning. Your filter choices are instantly applied to the active chat thread and are automatically saved so they persist across NetBeans IDE restarts. > [[Thinking and Tool Responses]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Chat Features]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Instead of creating temporary branches for minor changes or code drafts, you can save your progress as stashes and use the Stash Diff viewer as a visual sandbox: 1. Save your experimental code in a stash: `git stash`. 2. Open the NetBeans Git Repository Browser, select the stash, and press `Ctrl + Shift + L` (or click **Diff Stash** in the toolbar). 3. Simulate a merge by comparing it against **To HEAD**, or see how it fits with other local changes by comparing it against **To Working Tree**. 4. If you only want specific changes, right-click files in the diff list and choose **"Apply this change"** to cherry-pick them back into your working tree without applying the entire stash. > [[IDE Enhancements]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Auto-Backup on Turn Start]] > [[MCP Tools]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">IDE Enhancements</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The plugin integrates deeply with NetBeans beyond just the chat panel to boost your coding productivity: * **Markdown Project Type:** * Allows you to create a minimal project for managing folders of text notes, design files, or markdown documentation without requiring a compiler or build system (e.g., Maven or Gradle). * To create one, go to `Tools > New Project > Other > Markdown Project`. Alternatively, you can run `touch .mdproject` inside any folder to instantly make that directory loadable as a project in NetBeans. * It is identified by a `.mdproject` marker file, and renders a clean directory tree in the NetBeans Projects tab, automatically filtering out OS junk files and editor swap files. * You can close or delete the project directly from the right-click context menu on the project node. * **Stash Diff:** * A side-by-side diff viewer for git stashes. Select any stash in the NetBeans Git Repository Browser and press `Ctrl + Shift + L` (or click the **Diff Stash** button in the Git toolbar) to open it. * **To Base (default):** Displays stash parent commit vs stash content (equivalent to `git stash show -p`). * **To HEAD:** Simulates a 3-way merge applying the stash on your current HEAD, showing conflict markers inline (with a red "Conflict" label in the right panel if conflicts occur). * **To Working Tree:** Simulates applying the stash onto the working tree, showing unchanged/modified tree status on the left. * **File List & Partial Apply:** Click any file to view its syntax-highlighted diff, or right-click a file to "Apply this change" individually from the stash. * **Editor Context Menu Utilities:** * **Search Web:** Right-click selected text (or the word under the cursor) in the editor and click **Search Web** to quickly search Google using your NetBeans-configured web browser. * **Sort Lines Ascending / Descending:** Select multiple lines, right-click, and choose this option to alphabetically sort them. * **Minify JSON:** Right-click any JSON content to quickly strip out all formatting whitespace. * **Toggle Annotations:** Right-click in the editor and choose **Toggle Annotations** to toggle the versioning system's blame annotations for the file. * **View File History:** Right-click in the editor and choose **View File History** to open the versioning system's history view for the file. * Each of these context menu items can be enabled or disabled independently under `Tools > Options > Assistant`. * **Jump to File Dialog:** * A modeless file search dialog triggered via `Ctrl + Alt + J` (or `Cmd + Option + J` on Mac) that lets you search all open projects by filename prefix, path substring, or glob patterns. * Supports quick keyboard navigation with arrow keys and `Enter` to open. * Powered by an **In-Memory File Indexing Cache** that rebuilds in the background when projects are opened or closed. It automatically respects `.gitignore` rules and ignores common directories like `node_modules/`, `target/`, and `build/`. * Includes incremental live indexing via file system listeners, meaning new, deleted, or renamed files are immediately searchable without full rebuilds. * Can be enabled or disabled under `Tools > Options > Assistant`. > [[Markdown Project Type]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Jump to File]] > [[Send to Assistant]] > [[Inspector Context Menu]] / [[Test Results Context Menu]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] ---<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Keyboard Shortcuts</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Navigate and control the assistant efficiently using keyboard shortcuts: <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Shortcut</th><th>Action</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + L</code></td><td>Toggle the assistant panel (open or close)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Alt + Up</code> / <code>Alt + Down</code></td><td>Cycle through previously sent messages</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Page Up</code> / <code>Page Down</code></td><td>Scroll the chat</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + R</code></td><td>Search message history</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + Alt + J</code> (or <code>Cmd + Option + J</code> on Mac)</td><td>Open the Jump to File dialog</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + Shift + L</code></td><td>Open the Stash Diff viewer</td></tr> <tr><td><code>/</code></td><td>Open the slash command autocomplete popup</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Tab</code></td><td>Accept the highlighted autocomplete command and insert it into the input area</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Escape</code></td><td>Close the options panel</td></tr> </tbody> </table> > [[Input Area Keys]] > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Message History]] > [[Jump to File]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts Dialog]] > [[Expand/Collapse All]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Known Issues</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> - The plugin sometimes doesn't respond when using nested agents. - Switching sessions or reloading the conversation while awaiting a response can cancel the current request. - Permission requests from subagents (delegated agents) aren't always relayed by the ACP server back to the UI. If a subagent makes a tool call that requires permission, the request may hang and eventually time out because you never receive the Accept/Deny prompt. To mitigate this, directly instruct your primary agent to perform file modifications or commands rather than asking it to delegate those tasks to a subagent. > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Message History]] > [[Troubleshooting]] ---<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">macOS/Linux</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Use one of these options to install OpenCode - **macOS / Linux** (Recommended): <pre><code>`curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`</code></pre> - **NPM (Global):** <pre><code>`npm install -g opencode-ai`</code></pre> - **Homebrew (macOS):** <pre><code>`brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode`</code></pre> > [[Unix Config]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Local Data Analysis in Java</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> You can use the assistant to run quick data processing tasks on local files (like `.csv` or log files) using single-file Java programs and have the results rendered directly in the chat: 1. **Prepare your Data**: Open a project or create a folder with some tabular data (e.g., `sales.csv`). 2. **Ask the Assistant to Analyse**: Ask the assistant to write a single-file Java program to analyze this data. * *Prompt:* `"Write a single-file Java program to read sales.csv, calculate the total revenue grouped by category, and print the results as an ASCII table."` 3. **Execute the Code**: Click **Accept** on the permission prompt to let the assistant write the file (e.g., `SalesAnalyzer.java`) and run it using the Java launcher (e.g., `java SalesAnalyzer.java`). 4. **View Formatted Output**: Since Java 11+, single-file source code can be run directly using the `java` launcher without manual compilation. Because the plugin renders ASCII tables as formatted HTML tables with alternating row colors, the printed output will display beautifully inside your chat bubble. > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Thinking and Tool Responses]] > [[Experiments]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Since the plugin supports the **Markdown Project** type (which lets you load any folder that has a `.mdproject` file in it), you can use it to manage your OpenCode configuration directly inside the IDE: 1. Navigate to your OpenCode configuration directory in your terminal: * **Linux/macOS:** `~/.config/opencode` * **Windows:** `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode` 2. Create an empty project marker file by running: * `touch .mdproject` (Linux/macOS) * `type nul > .mdproject` (Windows CMD) or `New-Item .mdproject` (PowerShell) 3. Open NetBeans and go to `File > Open Project`. Navigate to that configuration directory and open it. 4. You can now manage your configuration directly inside the IDE. Since the files are loaded as a project in NetBeans, you can ask the assistant panel to make changes for you (e.g., "Add a new custom agent config to my opencode.json") instead of editing them manually. > [[Markdown Project Type]] > [[Configuration Template]] > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Message History</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> <img alt="Message history search" style="max-width:100%;"> Your complete message history is always safely stored on the server. While the local chat view hides older messages to conserve IDE memory, you can always retrieve the full history by clicking **Show All Messages** followed by **Reload** — the session is reloaded but all messages are retained. You can also search through your past input history using `Ctrl + R`. If you want to keep just one or two messages visible (e.g. a plan or to-do list), hover over the response bubble and click the pin icon; pinned messages stay in the chat panel instead of being cleared over time. > [[Pinned Messages]] > [[Input Area Keys]] > [[Exporting a conversation]] > [[Reloading a Session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Swing Mockups via Matisse</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> You can use the assistant to convert visual UI mockups (screenshots or wireframes) into Java Swing code, and enhance your Matisse GUI forms with custom components: 1. **Draft a Visual Mockup**: Draw a UI sketch or take a screenshot of a component you want to build. 2. **Generate the Custom Component**: Drag-and-drop the mockup image into the chat (or use the paperclip icon) and ask the assistant to code it. * *Prompt:* `"Analyze this mockup. Write a custom JComponent called GradientHeaderPanel.java that renders a color gradient background, a title label, and a drop shadow that matches this design."` 3. **Compile & Palette Import**: Let the assistant write the file, compile your project, and then drag the compiled `GradientHeaderPanel` class directly into the NetBeans **Matisse Palette**. 4. **Design visually with Matisse**: Open any Swing GUI form (like a `JFrame` or `JPanel`) in Matisse, and drag-and-drop your new custom AI-generated component directly from the Palette onto your form design. 5. **Hook up the Logic**: In your Matisse form, click the "Source" tab. Share the Matisse-generated class with the assistant and ask it to write the event listeners and backend logic for your visual components: * *Prompt:* `"Help me write the ActionListeners to connect the search button (btnSearch) to fetch results and populate the list model for lstResults."` > [[Attachments]] > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Experiments]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: alt="Permission Requests" style="max-width:100%;"> When the AI attempts to execute a tool, modify files, or run shell commands, the plugin ensures you remain in control. An Accept/Deny bubble will appear in the chat with full context of the requested action. You must explicitly grant permission before the operation proceeds. You can configure automatic allowances or denials in your OpenCode configuration. > [[Configuration Template]] > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Known Issues]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Hitting `Tab` when in the input text-area or pressing the small gear icon, will slide open the chat options panel, by default you'll see two agents build and plan, OpenCode also allows custom agents to be defined, pick one of the models supported by the providers you have configured, and a suitable Thinking Level, the actual levels displayed depend on the exact model selected. The gear would have turned into a down arrow button, click the button to close the options panel. You can also use the `/agents`, `/models`, and `/level` slash commands to open these selectors. > [[Commands]] / [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Input Area Keys]] > [[New Session Confirm Bar]] > alt="Assistant Options" style="max-width:100%;"> The plugin adds a tab to the NetBeans Options, if you open the Options Window, you'll see an additional Assistant tab at the end. In most cases, you can go with the defaults, but if you have a non-standard OpenCode installation, you can specify the full path to the OpenCode binary. The preamble is an additional user prompt that's sent to the server when creating a new chat session. The default text contains some directives around code quality, planning and task management, you can customise this with your own instructions. When you upgrade the NetBeans IDE to a new major version, the plugin automatically migrates your saved preferences and cached session data from the previous NetBeans user directory, so you do not need to reconfigure the assistant after an upgrade. > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Update Notifications]] > [[OpenCode Not Installed]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Renaming the session</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> To keep your conversations organised, you can rename any session. Click the **Pencil icon** in the chat UI or right-click a session in the session dropdown to give it a custom name. Alternatively, type the `/title` slash command to let the AI automatically generate and apply a suitable title based on the conversation context. These custom names are stored locally by the plugin, not in the OpenCode DB. > [[Session Dropdown Menu]] > [[Commands]] > [[Archiving Sessions]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Resetting context limits (/compact)</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If your conversation becomes very long and you notice the AI starting to forget earlier details or slow down as it approaches its context token limits, you can reset the conversation context. Type the `/compact` command in the chat input. The assistant will summarise the history, code changes, and context discussed so far, replacing the verbose message history with a highly condensed summary. This resets the active token budget while preserving the essential goals and context of the thread. > [[Commands]] / [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Check token usage]] > [[Reloading a Session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Restarting the server</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If the assistant becomes unresponsive or you experience connection issues, you can restart the underlying OpenCode background server. Click the **Restart ACP Server** button in the toolbar. This will safely terminate the current background process and spin up a new one, reconnecting your IDE without losing your saved sessions. > [[OpenCode Not Installed]] > [[Customising the Toolbar]] > alt="Assistant toolbar and input area for starting a session" style="max-width:100%;"> Click the '+' button on the toolbar to start a new session, this will initialise the chat interface and post the preamble to the OpenCode server (Tools > Options > Assistant > Preamble). The input text-area is at the bottom of the sidebar panel, you'll see placeholder text that says *Type Message Here*, type your messages and press `Enter` to send to the server, the response will be rendered as a chat bubble, if you need to send multi-line text, press `Shift + Enter` to add a newline to the text-area. You can also type `/new` in the input area to quickly start a new session. > [[New Session Confirm Bar]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] > [[Commands]] / [[Slash Command Autocomplete]] > [[Options Panel Reference]] > [[Input Area Keys]] > [[Welcome Screen]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Thinking and Tool Responses</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Advanced models use a "thinking" budget to reason before responding. This internal reasoning is displayed in its own collapsible pane. Similarly, when the AI uses tools, the tool output is shown in collapsible panes marked with a tag icon. You can use the **Filter** button to hide these thought or tool bubbles from the chat view, or use the **Expand/Collapse All** button to manage them all at once. By default, consecutive tool and thought bubbles are combined into a single expandable accordion, so you can collapse them together. You can turn this off under `Options > Assistant > Combine tool and thought bubbles into a single accordion`. Error messages will appear as red-tinted bubbles, and tables are rendered cleanly with alternating row colours. > [[Filtering Chat Messages]] > [[Time to first token]] > [[Auto-Backup on Turn Start]] space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Troubleshooting</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Problem</th><th>Solution</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><strong>Plugin can't find OpenCode</strong></td><td>Ensure <code>opencode</code> is on your <code>PATH</code>, or set the path manually under <code>Options &gt; Assistant</code>.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Assistant becomes unresponsive</strong></td><td>Click <strong>Restart ACP Server</strong> in the toolbar.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Ctrl + L stops working</strong></td><td>Close and reopen the assistant panel from the Window menu. If that doesn't work, restart the IDE.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Sidebar doesn't open after install/upgrade</strong></td><td>The plugin auto-opens the sidebar on version change. If it doesn't appear, open it from <code>Window &gt; Assistant</code>.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Image paste doesn't work with Wayland on Linux</strong></td><td>Install the <code>wl-clipboard</code> package (Wayland) or check your clipboard manager.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Image paste broken after OpenCode upgrade</strong></td><td>Upgrade to OpenCode &gt;= 1.17.17 to resolve the breakage introduced in v1.17.13.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Model not appearing after upgrade to OpenCode v1.17.9</strong>, upgrade plugin to &gt;= 1.7.3</td><td>Re-select your model via <code>/models</code>. The upgrade resets model selection due to the new <code>`thought_level`</code> split.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Session config payloads restructured after upgrade</strong></td><td>Upgrade the plugin to &gt;= 1.7.3 and OpenCode to &gt;= 1.17.17. Re-select your model and review any custom preamble or session settings.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Messages disappear from view</strong></td><td>This is display-only — the session still has all messages. Click <strong>Show All Messages</strong> to keep them visible, and use <strong>Reload</strong> to re-fetch from the server.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>LLM modified files unexpectedly</strong></td><td>It's a good idea to keep your project under version control (git), so you can easily revert any changes you don't want. You can also set OpenCode to 'ask' before editing, and review changes with the <strong>Allow Once/Always Allow/Reject</strong> permission prompts.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>High CPU usage or UI freezes</strong></td><td>Upgrade the plugin to &gt;= 1.9.2, which resolves an infinite layout validation loop in the chat panel.</td></tr> <tr><td><strong>Panel goes blank during docking or resizing</strong></td><td>Close and reopen the docked panel from <code>Window &gt; Assistant</code>. NetBeans may not repaint correctly after a drag-dock or undock operation.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> > [[OpenCode Not Installed]] > [[Restarting the server]] > [[Message History]] > [[Permission Requests]] > [[Known Issues]] > [[Auto-Reconnect]] > [[Reloading a Session]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Unix Config</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> On macOS/Linux, the OpenCode configuration is located at `$HOME/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. 1. Create this directory if it doesn't exist <pre><code>`mkdir -p $HOME/.config/opencode.`</code></pre> 2. Start your editor, whether it be `vi`, `nano` or any other. 3. Create the file `$HOME/.config/opencode/opencode.json` with the following template. > [[Configuration Template->Configuration Template]] Verify that the configuration is valid by running <pre><code>`opencode models`</code></pre> > [[After Installing OpenCode->Post Install]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Home</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> <i style="opacity: 0.7;">Last updated for BeanBot v1.16.0.</i> This guide will help you setup [[BeanBot]], a NetBeans plugin that provides an AI assistant panel powered by OpenCode, so you can chat with AI models directly inside the IDE. It automatically attaches active project and source file context to your messages, so the AI always understands what you're working on. It also features a built-in permission handler—allowing you to inspect code diffs before applying changes and explicitly approve file deletions or terminal commands. The plugin makes use of a new protocol called ACP (Agent Client Protocol) designed to let editors and IDEs like NetBeans interact with AI agents, we use OpenCode as an agent server, running it at IDE startup to send and receive messages from AI agents, this has the advantage that we don't have to add individual support for every AI provider like Anthropic, Gemini or OpenAI, OpenCode already supports multiple providers, and that makes it possible to switch between providers and models with ease. So the first thing we need to do is install OpenCode on your system and ensure the plugin can find it, pick the operating system you use from this list > [[macOS/Linux]] > [[Windows 10/11->Windows]] You should also look at the current documentation maintained at <a href="https://opencode.ai/download" target="_blank" rel="noopener">opencode.ai</a> To understand what the AI already knows about your code, read [[Automatic Context Capture]].<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Windows</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> On Windows, it is better to run OpenCode inside **WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)** for the best performance and compatibility. This allows it to execute regular bash commands. You can also use a package manager like chocolatey or scoop if you have them. To launch OpenCode through WSL from the plugin, enable **Launch through WSL** under `Tools > Options > Assistant > Assistant Service`. The plugin detects `wsl.exe` on your PATH and wraps all OpenCode invocations through WSL automatically, translating your Windows executable path to its WSL mount location. ##### Using the install script from WSL <pre><code>`curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`</code></pre> ##### Chocolatey <pre><code>`choco install opencode`</code></pre> ##### Scoop <pre><code>`scoop install opencode`</code></pre> > [[Windows Config]] > [[Options Panel Reference]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Windows Config</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> 1. Press WIN + R to open the Run dialog box. 2. Enter `cmd` for the Command Prompt. 3. The config directory might not exist, it can be created <pre><code> `mkdir "%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode" cd "%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode"` </code></pre> 4. Start `notepad` and paste in the starter configuration. > [[Configuration Template->Configuration Template]] Verify that the configuration is valid by running this from a command prompt <pre><code>`opencode models`</code></pre> > [[After Installing OpenCode->Post Install]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Opening the Mini Assistant</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> There are several ways to launch it: * **Toolbar button:** Click the **Mini Assistant** icon (a small chat bubble) in the assistant toolbar. This will dock the main panel and open the mini dialog. * **Keyboard shortcut:** Press `Ctrl + Alt + L` (or `Cmd + Alt + L` on Mac) to toggle it. * **Refactoring menu:** Right-click in the editor and choose **Ask Assistant** from the Refactoring menu. * **Code generation:** Press `Alt + Insert` (or the code generation shortcut for your platform) and select **Ask Assistant**. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Using the Mini Assistant]] > [[Keyboard shortcuts inside the Mini Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant Permission Requests]] > [[Differences from the main panel]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Using the Mini Assistant</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The dialog has a simple layout: a response display area on top and a text input at the bottom. Type your message and press `Enter` to send. Use `Shift + Enter` to add a newline without sending. While the AI is processing, a spinner and a token counter appear in the header so you can see progress in real time. The latest response is displayed as a compact bubble with a reduced font size. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Opening the Mini Assistant]] > [[Keyboard shortcuts inside the Mini Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant Permission Requests]] > [[Differences from the main panel]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Keyboard shortcuts inside the Mini Assistant</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Shortcut</th><th>Action</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><code>Enter</code></td><td>Send message</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Shift + Enter</code></td><td>New line</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Tab</code></td><td>Slash command autocomplete</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Page Up / Page Down</code></td><td>Navigate between response bubbles</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + C</code></td><td>Copy code block or full text</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + L</code></td><td>Toggle the main assistant panel</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ctrl + Alt + L</code></td><td>Toggle the mini assistant itself</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Escape</code></td><td>Close popups, then close the dialog</td></tr> </tbody> </table> When you navigate away from the latest bubble using Page Up/Down, auto-tracking pauses until you return to the newest response. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Opening the Mini Assistant]] > [[Using the Mini Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant Permission Requests]] > [[Differences from the main panel]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Mini Assistant Permission Requests</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If the AI requests permission to edit a file or run a command, the permission prompt appears directly inside the mini dialog. You can Allow or Deny the request, and for file edits, a **Show Diff** button lets you inspect the changes before approving. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Opening the Mini Assistant]] > [[Using the Mini Assistant]] > [[Keyboard shortcuts inside the Mini Assistant]] > [[Differences from the main panel]] > [[Permission Requests]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Differences from the main panel</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The mini assistant is designed for quick interactions. Some slash commands that require the full options panel (`/model`, `/models`, `/agents`, `/level`, `/sessions`) are not available in the mini view — use the main panel or its keyboard shortcuts for those. The dialog remembers its position and size across sessions, so you can place it wherever is convenient in your workspace. > [[Mini Assistant]] > [[Opening the Mini Assistant]] > [[Using the Mini Assistant]] > [[Keyboard shortcuts inside the Mini Assistant]] > [[Mini Assistant Permission Requests]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Install Ollama</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> [Ollama](https://ollama.com) lets you run open-source models locally on your own machine. The first step is installing it. Download the installer for your operating system from the [Ollama website](https://ollama.com/download) and run it. On Linux you can also use the install script: <pre><code> curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh </code></pre> On macOS, Ollama installs as a regular app — launch it once so the background service starts. **Windows (10 or later)** is also supported: install via the standalone `OllamaSetup.exe` download, or run the PowerShell installer: <pre><code> irm https://ollama.com/install.ps1 | iex </code></pre> Verify the installation by opening a terminal (or PowerShell on Windows) and running: <pre><code> ollama --version </code></pre> Once the `ollama` command responds, move on to fetching a coding model. > [[Fetch a Coding Model]] > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Fetch a Coding Model</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> With Ollama installed, open a terminal and pull a model suited for code. Good options include: <pre><code> ollama pull deepseek-coder ollama pull qwen2.5-coder ollama pull codellama ollama pull llama3.1 </code></pre> The first run of `ollama run <model>` will download the model if it is not already present. You can see what is installed at any time with: <pre><code> ollama list </code></pre> Remember the exact model names shown by `ollama list` — you will need them when [[configuring OpenCode->Configure OpenCode for Ollama]]. > [[Install Ollama]] > [[Configure OpenCode for Ollama]] > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Configure OpenCode for Ollama</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> OpenCode needs to know which provider serves the local model. Open your `opencode.json` configuration file (see [[Configuration Template]] for where this file lives) and add an `ollama` entry to its `provider` section. The rest of your existing file — permissions, etc. — stays untouched, so it looks something like this: <pre><code> ` { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "autoupdate": false, "permission": { ... }, "provider": { "ollama": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/ollama", "options": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:11434/api" }, "models": { "deepseek-coder": {}, "qwen2.5-coder": {} } } } } ` </code></pre> The `...` stands for whatever permissions and other settings your file already has — keep them, and add the `provider` block alongside them. The exact `models` entries must match the names shown by `ollama list` from the previous step. Qwen models may require `"reasoningEffort": "none"` and `--think=false` if they are configured via Ollama. Once the provider block is in place, select the model in the plugin. > [[Fetch a Coding Model]] > [[Select the Model in the Plugin]] > [[Configuration Template]] > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Select the Model in the Plugin</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> After [[configuring OpenCode->Configure OpenCode for Ollama]], pick your local model in the plugin: 1. Click the gear icon (or press `Tab` in the input area) to open the chat options panel. 2. Pick the **agent** you want to use (e.g. `build` or `plan`). 3. Pick your **model** from the model dropdown — the local models configured above will appear there, listed as their provider/model names. 4. Choose a suitable **Thinking Level** if the model supports one. Every query and indexing task now runs entirely on your machine — no data leaves your computer. See [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]] for privacy notes and [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] for more on the selectors. > [[Configure OpenCode for Ollama]] > [[Offline/Private Coding (Local LLMs)]] > [[Picking an Agent, Model and Thinking Level]] > [[Options Panel Reference]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">MCP Tools</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The plugin runs a small built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server inside the IDE and exposes it to the OpenCode agent server. When the agent supports MCP, it can call a handful of NetBeans tools directly during your conversation — you don't have to switch to the IDE and click around: <table class="ug-table"> <thead><tr><th>Tool</th><th>What it does</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td><code>get&#95;tabs</code></td><td>Lists the file paths currently open in editor tabs (only files inside your open projects).</td></tr> <tr><td><code>open&#95;pos</code></td><td>Opens a file at a given line number in the editor and focuses it. Useful when the AI says "Show me where this happens in the code".</td></tr> <tr><td><code>list&#95;projects</code></td><td>Lists the absolute paths of all open NetBeans projects.</td></tr> <tr><td><code>rename&#95;session</code></td><td>Gives the current (or a specific) session a custom title, just like the rename button.</td></tr> <tr><td><code>diff&#95;stash</code></td><td>Opens the side-by-side stash diff viewer for a given stash. Only available when Stash Diff is enabled in Options.</td></tr> </tbody> </table> The MCP server binds to <code>127.0.0.1</code> on a random local port with a random token, so it never accepts connections from outside your machine. It only activates when your agent server advertises MCP support. When the AI uses one of these tools, the call and its result appear in the chat as a collapsible tool bubble with the tag icon — same as any other tool output. > [[Thinking and Tool Responses]] > [[Git Stashes as "Code Drafts" (using Stash Diff)]] > [[Renaming the session]] > [[Automatic Context Capture]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Automatic Context Capture</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Every message you send automatically carries supplementary context about your current editor state, so the AI knows what you are working on without you having to explain it. For the active editor this includes: - the file path of the open document - the selected text and its line range, when you have a selection - the current cursor line Your open projects are attached as well, so the AI knows the boundaries of your project. This context is reference-only metadata — your typed message is always the primary input. If no real file is open (for example an empty editor or a temporary document), no phantom path like <code>/tmp/xxx</code> is sent, so the AI is never confused by made-up file locations. This is what powers the MCP <code>open&#95;pos</code> and <code>get&#95;tabs</code> tools, which let the AI jump you to the exact file and line it is talking about. > [[Home]] > [[MCP Tools]] > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Chat Features]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Reloading a Session</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The **Reload** button (reload icon) on the toolbar re-fetches the current session from the OpenCode server. Your messages are always stored on the server, so reloading never loses anything — it just refreshes the chat view to match the server state. You'll want to reload when: - you ran <code>/compact</code> and want the summarised history displayed - older messages were trimmed from the view (click **Show All Messages** first, then **Reload** to bring them all back) - the view seems out of sync with the server, for example after a server restart or a session reload from the dropdown > [[Message History]] > [[Resetting context limits (/compact)]] > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Restarting the server]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Welcome Screen</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> When the assistant panel is opened with no session selected, you'll see the welcome screen instead of a chat thread. It shows a **Start New Chat** button plus a list of your existing sessions, each with the project folder it belongs to shown underneath the title. Click any session to open it, or **Start New Chat** to begin a fresh conversation. Sessions you have archived (hidden) are only listed when hidden sessions are visible — use the eye icon on the toolbar to toggle them. > [[Starting a Session]] > [[Session Dropdown Menu]] > [[Archiving Sessions]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Auto-Reconnect</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> If the OpenCode server process dies or its pipes break mid-conversation, the plugin handles it automatically: 1. any stale server process is killed and its connections closed 2. a notification appears: **ACP Server Disconnected — Attempting to reconnect...** 3. the server is restarted automatically with a short backoff (about 3, 6, then 9 seconds) The plugin gives up after **3 failed restarts within 5 minutes** and shows a "server crashed" status message. In that case check your OpenCode installation, then click **Restart ACP Server** to try again. Your sessions are not lost during a reconnect — they are stored on the server and simply reloaded. > [[Restarting the server]] > [[Troubleshooting]] > [[OpenCode Not Installed]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Expand/Collapse All</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Thoughts, tool outputs and code blocks are rendered as collapsible panes so a long assistant response stays readable. Instead of opening or closing them one by one, use the **Expand/Collapse All** toolbar button to toggle every block in the chat at once. The button icon and tooltip switch between *Expand All* and *Collapse All* so you always know what the next click will do. It's handy right after streaming finishes — collapse everything to see the final summary, or expand everything to inspect every tool result. > [[Thinking and Tool Responses]] > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Filtering Chat Messages]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Keyboard Shortcuts Dialog</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> Click the keyboard icon in the assistant panel header to open the **Keyboard Shortcuts** dialog. It lists every shortcut the plugin supports, grouped by section — Navigation &amp; Assistant, Session Management, Chat Input, Editing and Stash Diff — with the keys rendered as keyboard badges. Type in the filter field at the top to search by key or action name. Shortcuts that are not currently assigned are collapsed into a single clickable *Unassigned* summary row per section; click it to expand the full list. Press <code>Escape</code> to close the dialog. > [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] > [[Customising the Toolbar]] > [[Input Area Keys]]<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 1rem;"> <div style="font-weight: bold; text-align: left; flex-grow: 1;">Global Configuration Setup</div> <div>[[Index->Topic Index]]</div> </div> The first time you start the assistant (and on server restarts), the plugin checks for a global OpenCode configuration file at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (or `opencode.jsonc`). This file holds security settings like file-permission rules and which commands require your approval. If the file is missing, empty, or contains only the `$schema` reference, the chat panel shows a prompt offering to write a starter configuration: * **Set up starter config** — writes the bundled starter file (see [[Configuration Template]]) to your config directory. * **Not now** — defers the prompt for the current IDE session. It won't ask again until you restart the IDE. If an existing file can't be parsed, the prompt instead asks whether to **Replace** it (which overwrites the broken file) or **Keep** it unchanged. Files that already contain real configuration are never touched. When a config prompt was shown, a confirmation hint with an **OK** button appears before the server starts — click it to proceed. The hint also points you to `opencode auth login` and the free models at **Opencode Zen** (https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/) if you haven't added a model provider yet. > [[Configuration Template]] > [[Manage OpenCode Config in NetBeans]] > [[OpenCode Not Installed]] > [[Post Install]] > [[Restarting the server]]
